findings.claim: CFTC Staff Letter 26-17 explicitly lists XRP as an example of a digital commodity and provides a conditional staff no-action path for CFM customer-owned digital commodities and payment stablecoins to be transferred through CBBM to Deribit for 30.7 customer foreign-futures/foreign-option margin under a right of re-use.
Deribit's September 28 cross-collateral table lists XRP as a full cross-collateral currency and an offset currency, with no stated X:PM haircut and a 15% X:SM haircut.
Deribit lists an XRP-USDC linear perpetual; the contract is USDC-settled and can use cross collateral when the account's margin mode supports it.
Coinbase states the International Exchange/Deribit integration completed October 1, 2026 and that perpetual trading infrastructure moved onto Deribit.

The combination of CFTC 26-17, XRP's named digital-commodity status, Deribit's current XRP cross-collateral eligibility and Coinbase's completed integration establishes a credible institutional route through which XRP can support derivatives margin beyond XRP-only positions, subject to account eligibility, CFM's notice/three-month restrictions, venue settings and applicable haircuts.

CFM's actual notice-of-intent date, commencement date, expiry of its initial three-month restriction, U.S. customer access to XRP cross collateral, posted XRP balances, actual reuse, account-level haircuts and custody balances were not verified.

CFTC 26-05 initially restricts an FCM to payment stablecoins, BTC and ETH for the first three months from its own commencement date. The CFTC letters are conditional staff positions, not blanket rulemaking; Deribit platform specifications do not prove CFM account enablement or actual usage.

Collateral eligibility can improve capital efficiency and reduce the need to liquidate already-held XRP to fund derivatives margin, but it does not establish new spot purchases or net external capital inflows.

If materially adopted, XRP cross collateral could increase demand to hold XRP for multi-asset derivatives margin, but the magnitude, direction and price effect are unknown and may be offset by rehypothecation, liquidation and counterparty risks.

competing_hypotheses.statement: CFM has enabled XRP as customer collateral for eligible U.S. 30.7 customers through CBBM/Deribit after satisfying the notice and initial-period requirements.
disconfirming: No CFM notice date, account configuration, actual posted balance or weekly asset report was found.
competing_hypotheses.test: Locate CFM's WinJammer notice, relevant disclosures and independently verifiable collateral balance/flow data.

competing_hypotheses.statement: The legal and venue framework permits XRP collateral in principle, but CFM has not enabled or materially used XRP in U.S. customer accounts.
support: No actual balance or use evidence found; venue eligibility alone is not usage.
disconfirming: Coinbase/Deribit integration is complete and XRP is on Deribit's current cross-collateral table.
competing_hypotheses.test: Monitor CFM product disclosures, customer eligibility notices and venue/FCM collateral reports.

competing_hypotheses.statement: Any XRP collateral adoption mostly reuses existing holdings and improves capital efficiency without creating comparable net spot buying.
support: The CFTC framework is based on customer-owned assets; no purchase is required merely to post existing XRP.
disconfirming: New account onboarding or portfolio requirements could create incremental acquisition demand, but this is not measured.
competing_hypotheses.test: Compare collateral balances, net deposits, venue spot flows, custody changes and price/volume around verified adoption events.

explicit_non_equivalences: Digital-commodity classification is not the same as actual FCM acceptance.
Deribit cross-collateral eligibility is not proof of CFM U.S. account enablement.
Collateral posted is not necessarily newly purchased XRP.
A right of re-use is not proof that assets were actually rehypothecated.
Deribit margin haircuts are not the same as CFTC FCM capital charges or DCO initial-margin requirements.
